---
title: "JQI_PolAttitudes_Race_Controls"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
# ============================================================
# POLITICAL ATTITUDES BY RACE:
# WHITE, BLACK, AND HISPANIC RESPONDENTS
#
# Purpose:
# Examine whether the relationships between the three JQI
# components and political attitudes remain within White,
# Black, and Hispanic respondents after controlling for:
#
#   - employment status
#   - subjective social class
#   - occupational prestige
#   - income
#   - age
#   - sex
#   - education
#   - political ideology
#   - party identification
#
# This is a descriptive stratified analysis.
# No model-fit comparisons are conducted.
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(MASS)
library(broom)


# ============================================================
# 1. PREPARE RACE VARIABLE
# ============================================================

jqi_political_race <- jqi_political %>%
  mutate(

    race_group_3 = case_when(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 1 ~ "White",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 2 ~ "Black",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 16 ~ "Hispanic",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    race_group_3 = factor(
      race_group_3,
      levels = c(
        "White",
        "Black",
        "Hispanic"
      )
    ),

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Political ideology
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    polviews_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(polviews)),

    polviews_factor = case_when(
      polviews_num %in% 1:7 ~ polviews_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    polviews_factor = factor(
      polviews_factor,
      levels = 1:7,
      labels = c(
        "Extremely liberal",
        "Liberal",
        "Slightly liberal",
        "Moderate",
        "Slightly conservative",
        "Conservative",
        "Extremely conservative"
      )
    ),

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Party identification
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    party_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(partyid)),

    party_factor = case_when(
      party_num %in% 0:7 ~ party_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    party_factor = factor(
      party_factor,
      levels = 0:7,
      labels = c(
        "Strong Democrat",
        "Not very strong Democrat",
        "Independent, close to Democrat",
        "Independent",
        "Independent, close to Republican",
        "Not very strong Republican",
        "Strong Republican",
        "Other party"
      )
    ),

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Sex
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    sex_factor = case_when(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)) == 1 ~ "Male",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)) == 2 ~ "Female",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    sex_factor = factor(
      sex_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Male",
        "Female"
      )
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 2. CHECK RACIAL SAMPLE SIZES
# ============================================================

table(
  jqi_political_race$race_group_3,
  useNA = "ifany"
)


# ============================================================
# 3. FUNCTION TO RUN FULL CONTROLLED MODEL
# ============================================================

run_race_stratified_model <- function(data, outcome, race_value) {

  formula_text <- paste0(
    outcome,
    " ~ ",
    "wrkstat_factor + ",
    "social_class_factor + ",
    "compensation + ",
    "benefits + ",
    "earnings_stability + ",
    "prestige + ",
    "log_realrinc + ",
    "age + ",
    "sex_factor + ",
    "educ + ",
    "polviews_factor + ",
    "party_factor"
  )

  model_formula <- as.formula(formula_text)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Restrict to racial group
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  group_data <- data %>%
    filter(
      race_group_3 == race_value
    )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Identify variables needed by model
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  model_vars <- all.vars(model_formula)

  model_data <- group_data %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(model_vars)) %>%
    na.omit() %>%
    droplevels()

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Check outcome variation
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if (
    nrow(model_data) == 0 ||
    length(unique(model_data[[outcome]])) < 2
  ) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit ordered logit
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  model <- MASS::polr(
    model_formula,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract coefficients
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  results <- broom::tidy(model) %>%
    mutate(
      outcome = outcome,
      race = race_value,
      n = nrow(model_data),
      p.value = 2 * pnorm(
        abs(statistic),
        lower.tail = FALSE
      )
    )

  list(
    model = model,
    results = results,
    data = model_data
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 4. RUN MODELS FOR ALL OUTCOMES × RACE GROUPS
# ============================================================

political_outcomes <- c(
  "eqwlth",
  "getahead",
  "kidssol",
  "poleff11",
  "tax"
)

race_groups <- c(
  "White",
  "Black",
  "Hispanic"
)


race_stratified_models <- list()

for (r in race_groups) {

  for (o in political_outcomes) {

    model_name <- paste(
      r,
      o,
      sep = "_"
    )

    race_stratified_models[[model_name]] <-
      run_race_stratified_model(
        jqi_political_race,
        o,
        r
      )
  }
}


# ============================================================
# 5. COMBINE ALL RESULTS
# ============================================================

race_stratified_results <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    race_stratified_models,
    function(x) {

      if (is.null(x)) {
        return(NULL)
      }

      x$results
    }
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 6. JQI COMPONENT RESULTS
# ============================================================

jqi_race_results <- race_stratified_results %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "compensation",
      "benefits",
      "earnings_stability"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    race,
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    race,
    term
  )

print(jqi_race_results)


# ============================================================
# 7. RACE-SPECIFIC JQI RESULTS IN WIDE FORMAT
#
# Easier for directly comparing the three groups.
# ============================================================

jqi_race_wide <- jqi_race_results %>%
  mutate(
    estimate_se = sprintf(
      "%.3f (%.3f)",
      estimate,
      std.error
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    race,
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate_se,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = race,
    values_from = estimate_se
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    term
  )

jqi_race_wide


# ============================================================
# 8. SAVE JQI RESULTS
# ============================================================

write.csv(
  jqi_race_results,
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "political_attitudes_JQI_White_Black_Hispanic.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  jqi_race_wide,
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "political_attitudes_JQI_White_Black_Hispanic_wide.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# 9. DEMOGRAPHIC / CONTROL RESULTS
#
# Useful if you want to see how the racial groups differ after
# conditioning on the same set of covariates.
# ============================================================

control_terms <- c(
  "prestige",
  "log_realrinc",
  "age",
  "sex_factorFemale",
  "education"
)

control_results <- race_stratified_results %>%
  filter(
    term %in% control_terms
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    race,
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    race,
    term
  )

print(control_results)


# ============================================================
# 10. IDEOLOGY RESULTS
# ============================================================

ideology_results <- race_stratified_results %>%
  filter(
    grepl(
      "^polviews_factor",
      term
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    race,
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    race,
    term
  )

print(ideology_results)


# ============================================================
# 11. PARTY ID RESULTS
# ============================================================

party_results <- race_stratified_results %>%
  filter(
    grepl(
      "^party_factor",
      term
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    race,
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    n
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    race,
    term
  )

print(party_results)


# ============================================================
# 12. SAMPLE SIZE TABLE
#
# This is especially important for Hispanic respondents because
# some outcomes have substantially smaller complete-case samples.
# ============================================================

race_sample_sizes <- race_stratified_results %>%
  dplyr::select(
    race,
    outcome,
    n
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(
    outcome,
    race
  )

print(race_sample_sizes)

write.csv(
  race_sample_sizes,
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "political_attitudes_White_Black_Hispanic_sample_sizes.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
